title: London Update -- Young Straw Admits to Selling Hash; Says He Has Learned His Lesson -- But His Father Still Hasn't

content_html_sanitized:
LONDON

William Straw, 17,  admitted to police Monday that he sold hashish to a newspaper reporter. He was accompanied to the station by his father, Home Secretary Jack Straw and signed a form admitting the offense and agreeing to an "official warning," which will be deleted from his record if he commits no further offenses for three years.

On Dec. 24, The Mirror reporter Dawn Alford said she posed as a real estate agent in training looking for drugs, and struck up a conversation with the youth in a London pub and bought .07 ounces of hashish for $16.50 from the young Straw. Alford, 30, was later charged with possession of the hashish. But Scotland Yard said Monday that she had been notified that no further action would be taken.

When the paper informed the senior Straw, he took his son to the police station where he was arrested and released without bail. The father said he hoped that young William will not suffer additionally ``simply because he is my son.'' (Being his son is certainly punishment enough.) He then went on to say that ``William is now learning the lessons of this episode and he, of course, has my support in doing so."

The real question is whether the father has learned anything. Judging by his public statements, it does not appear that he has. Straw said he had no intention of resigning, and Prime Minister Tony Blair has given him his full support.

In any case, Oxford University has informed William that he will still be able to enter New College later this year. All's well that ends well. Why change the laws? Nothing bad happens to people who are arrested. They all just go to Oxford. (By the way, if marijuana is so dangerous, how did the kid get into Oxford? )
